source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Florida Department of Health (FDOH) arbovirus surveillance reports, weekly or monthly situation reports, and press releases reporting dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Florida during June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDOH is the primary official source for dengue case counts in Florida, publishing arbovirus surveillance summaries that include travel-associated and locally acquired dengue cases by county.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC Division of Vector-Borne Diseases (DVBD) reports, tables, or dashboards containing dengue case data for Florida for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and may contain Florida-specific dengue case counts, including confirmed and probable classifications.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level health department reports (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange) with dengue case data for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-population Florida counties with international travel hubs are most likely to report dengue cases; county health departments may publish local arbovirus alerts or situation reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO or WHO situation reports, disease outbreak news, or regional surveillance bulletins referencing dengue in Florida or the USA for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent validation of case counts and can confirm whether Florida-specific data is included in broader US or Americas summaries.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (HealthMap, ProMED, Global Health Monitor, or open data portals) with dengue event records for Florida in June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured surveillance databases aggregate official and news signals and can serve as independent validation against FDOH and CDC primary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC case definitions establishing dengue confirmed, probable, and suspected classification criteria applicable to Florida surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition context is required to correctly interpret and normalize case classification fields (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) extracted from FDOH and CDC sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify background sources describing Florida's dengue epidemiology, including travel-associated vs. locally acquired case patterns, to contextualize June 2025 data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Florida dengue cases are predominantly travel-associated; understanding this baseline helps flag anomalies such as locally acquired clusters or outbreaks.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where dengue counts are aggregated with other arboviruses (West Nile, Zika, chikungunya) without dengue-specific breakdowns, or where reporting period substantially exceeds June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Arbovirus aggregate counts without dengue-specific figures must not be extracted as dengue records; sources with broad reporting periods require human judgment on date-window fit.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite case counts without traceable official provenance for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified figures; human review ensures only traceable, provenance-backed counts enter the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: FDOH publishes weekly and annual arbovirus surveillance reports including dengue case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable), travel status, and occasionally hospitalizations and deaths. CDC DVBD and ArboNET provide national-level data with state breakdowns. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for Florida dengue in June 2025.

PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological updates covering the Americas including the USA. WHO Disease Outbreak News may reference US dengue events. These provide independent validation of Florida case data.

HealthMap, ProMED-mail, Global Health Monitor, and open government data portals aggregate dengue event signals from official and news sources. These structured databases can validate FDOH/CDC primary data and surface county-level signals.

Peer-reviewed studies on Florida dengue epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology provide context for interpreting extracted counts. Recent publications may also contain 2025 case series or outbreak reports.

Local Florida news outlets (Miami Herald, Tampa Bay Times, Sun Sentinel) and health news aggregators may report dengue alerts, locally acquired case clusters, or FDOH press releases during June 2025, providing early signals and supporting evidence quotes.

Useful for identifying specific localities, dates, and case counts cited from official sources, and for discovering links to primary official reports. Refines upstream q_exec_009 with natural language time reference and without unnatural date-range string.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News article, press release, or health alert from June 2025 reporting dengue cases in Florida, ideally citing FDOH or CDC figures with specific case counts, county-level data, or death/hospitalization information.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Bylined journalism citing official health agency sources, press releases from FDOH or county health departments, publication date within June 2025.

expected_evidence: FDOH arboviral/dengue surveillance report with statewide or county-level case counts for June 2025
CDC ArboNET or CDC dengue statistics page with Florida 2025 case data
PAHO situation report referencing US/Florida dengue cases for June 2025
News articles citing official case counts, deaths, or hospitalizations for Florida dengue in June 2025
Tabular data with confirmed/probable/suspected case breakdowns
Evidence quotes with specific numbers, dates, and locations
expected_source_characteristics: Official Florida state health agency authorship (FDOH)
CDC national surveillance program (ArboNET)
International health organization (PAHO/WHO) situation reports
Publication or report date within or immediately after June 2025
Quantitative case count data with geographic and temporal specificity
English-language documents from .gov, .paho.org, or .who.int domains
search_iteration_plans.language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. Florida is a US state; all official reporting from FDOH, CDC, and PAHO for this jurisdiction is in English. No Spanish-language queries are needed for this iteration, as the target is US state-level official reporting. Spanish-language queries could be considered in a future iteration only if seeking travel-origin country reports, which is out of scope for this task.
trust_considerations: Prioritize FDOH and CDC as primary authoritative sources for Florida dengue data
PAHO/WHO reports provide independent international validation
News sources are supplementary; only accept case counts that cite official agency sources
Avoid sources that do not specify Florida as the location or that aggregate US data without state breakdown
Be alert to travel-associated vs. locally-acquired dengue distinctions, which FDOH typically reports separately
Verify that report dates or data periods overlap with June 2025 (2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30)
search_iteration_plans.stop_condition_hypothesis: Stop after iteration 1 if queries return FDOH surveillance reports and CDC ArboNET data with quantified case counts, dates, and locality data for June 2025. Proceed to iteration 2 if official agency sources are absent, data is incomplete (e.g., missing deaths/hospitalizations/locality), or only news sources are found without official backing.
warnings: Upstream planned queries used unnatural date-range strings (e.g., '2025-06-01-2025-06-30') unlikely to match real document text — all iteration 1 queries use natural language time references instead
Peer-reviewed literature queries (upstream q_exec_005/q_exec_006) are deprioritized: publication lag makes June 2025 literature extremely unlikely to exist in iteration 1
Structured database queries (upstream q_exec_007/q_exec_008) are deferred to iteration 2 if official agency sources are insufficient
Florida dengue cases are predominantly travel-associated; locally-acquired cases are rarer and may be reported separately — both categories should be captured
FDOH may use 'arboviral disease' as the umbrella category rather than 'dengue' alone in report titles

iterative_search_queries.query: Florida Department of Health dengue arboviral surveillance report June 2025
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: FDOH is the primary authoritative source for Florida dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and locality data. Targeting FDOH surveillance reports with natural-language time reference 'June 2025' and disease-specific term 'arboviral' (FDOH uses this umbrella term for dengue reporting) maximizes retrieval of the most relevant official documents. This replaces the upstream q_exec_001/q_exec_002 which used an unnatural date-range string unlikely to match document text.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Florida Department of Health (.fdoh.gov or .myflorida.com domain), official surveillance program authorship, tabular case count data with date ranges.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC ArboNET dengue cases Florida 2025 surveillance data
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system that aggregates state-reported dengue data including Florida. CDC also publishes dengue case counts by state. This query targets CDC's dengue surveillance pages and ArboNET data tables, which may include June 2025 Florida case counts, confirmed/probable breakdowns, and deaths. Complements FDOH data and provides cross-validation.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC dengue surveillance summary, ArboNET data table, or CDC dengue statistics page showing Florida case counts for 2025 (ideally broken down by month or including June).
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: CDC.gov domain, ArboNET program attribution, tabular state-level case count data.

count_semantics_notes: Strictly separate locally acquired (autochthonous) cases from travel-associated (imported) cases — Florida frequently reports both categories.
Dengue reports commonly use epidemiological (epi) weeks; map epi week to calendar date range for the 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30 window (Epi Weeks 22–26 approximately).
Cumulative year-to-date counts must be distinguished from period-specific (June 2025) counts.
Confirmed vs. probable case definitions may differ between FDOH and CDC ArboNET; record the definition used.
County-level counts should be recorded separately from statewide totals when both are available.
Do not aggregate dengue counts with other arboviral diseases (Zika, chikungunya, West Nile) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly broken out.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arbovirus counts (e.g., combined Zika + dengue + chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly reported.
Do not treat mosquito surveillance positivity (Aedes trap data) as human case counts.
Florida reports may include both travel-associated and locally acquired dengue — do not conflate these categories.
DENV serotype data (DENV-1 through DENV-4) should not be counted as separate case events.
ArboNET national totals must not be substituted for Florida-specific counts.
Hospitalization figures from clinical databases (e.g., discharge records) may differ from FDOH surveillance counts — note the source definition.
exclusion_terms: Aedes trap data without human cases
warnings: Florida dengue reports frequently distinguish travel-associated from locally acquired cases — both categories must be captured and labeled separately in collection records.
Epi week boundaries for June 2025 (approx. Epi Weeks 22–26) must be mapped to calendar dates before populating date_reported fields.
FDOH arbovirus surveillance reports may be published with a 1–2 week lag; the June 30 end date may not yet have a corresponding published report at time of collection.
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates — always filter or confirm Florida-specific figures before recording.
County-level dengue data may be suppressed in public FDOH reports for small counts (n<5) to protect patient privacy; record suppression explicitly rather than imputing zero.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Florida Department of Health (FDOH) arbovirus surveillance reports, weekly or monthly situation reports, and press releases reporting dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Florida during June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDOH is the primary official source for dengue case counts in Florida, publishing arbovirus surveillance summaries that include travel-associated and locally acquired dengue cases by county.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC Division of Vector-Borne Diseases (DVBD) reports, tables, or dashboards containing dengue case data for Florida for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and may contain Florida-specific dengue case counts, including confirmed and probable classifications.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level health department reports (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange) with dengue case data for June 2025.

Complements FDOH data and provides cross-validation.

input.user_request: Collect dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Florida from 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30.

structured_task.user_request: Collect dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Florida from 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30.

collection_spec.data_focus: human Dengue case, outbreak, and surveillance data
collection_spec.user_request: Collect dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Florida from 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30.

official_source_terms: Florida Department of Health arbovirus surveillance
likely_reporting_agencies: county health departments (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange)
count_semantics_notes: Strictly separate locally acquired (autochthonous) cases from travel-associated (imported) cases — Florida frequently reports both categories.
Dengue reports commonly use epidemiological (epi) weeks; map epi week to calendar date range for the 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30 window (Epi Weeks 22–26 approximately).
Cumulative year-to-date counts must be distinguished from period-specific (June 2025) counts.
Confirmed vs. probable case definitions may differ between FDOH and CDC ArboNET; record the definition used.
County-level counts should be recorded separately from statewide totals when both are available.
Do not aggregate dengue counts with other arboviral diseases (Zika, chikungunya, West Nile) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly broken out.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arbovirus counts (e.g., combined Zika + dengue + chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly reported.
Do not treat mosquito surveillance positivity (Aedes trap data) as human case counts.
Florida reports may include both travel-associated and locally acquired dengue — do not conflate these categories.
DENV serotype data (DENV-1 through DENV-4) should not be counted as separate case events.
ArboNET national totals must not be substituted for Florida-specific counts.
Hospitalization figures from clinical databases (e.g., discharge records) may differ from FDOH surveillance counts — note the source definition.
exclusion_terms: Aedes trap data without human cases
warnings: Florida dengue reports frequently distinguish travel-associated from locally acquired cases — both categories must be captured and labeled separately in collection records.
Epi week boundaries for June 2025 (approx. Epi Weeks 22–26) must be mapped to calendar dates before populating date_reported fields.
FDOH arbovirus surveillance reports may be published with a 1–2 week lag; the June 30 end date may not yet have a corresponding published report at time of collection.
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates — always filter or confirm Florida-specific figures before recording.
County-level dengue data may be suppressed in public FDOH reports for small counts (n<5) to protect patient privacy; record suppression explicitly rather than imputing zero.

Do not invent or assume URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed, verifiable source documents.

If PAHO or WHO situation reports reference U.S. dengue counts, confirm whether Florida is explicitly named before attributing counts to this geography.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Florida Department of Health (FDOH) arbovirus surveillance reports, weekly or monthly situation reports, and press releases reporting dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Florida during June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDOH is the primary official source for dengue case counts in Florida, publishing arbovirus surveillance summaries that include travel-associated and locally acquired dengue cases by county.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC Division of Vector-Borne Diseases (DVBD) reports, tables, or dashboards containing dengue case data for Florida for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and may contain Florida-specific dengue case counts, including confirmed and probable classifications.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level health department reports (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange) with dengue case data for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-population Florida counties with international travel hubs are most likely to report dengue cases; county health departments may publish local arbovirus alerts or situation reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO or WHO situation reports, disease outbreak news, or regional surveillance bulletins referencing dengue in Florida or the USA for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent validation of case counts and can confirm whether Florida-specific data is included in broader US or Americas summaries.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (HealthMap, ProMED, Global Health Monitor, or open data portals) with dengue event records for Florida in June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured surveillance databases aggregate official and news signals and can serve as independent validation against FDOH and CDC primary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC case definitions establishing dengue confirmed, probable, and suspected classification criteria applicable to Florida surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition context is required to correctly interpret and normalize case classification fields (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) extracted from FDOH and CDC sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify background sources describing Florida's dengue epidemiology, including travel-associated vs. locally acquired case patterns, to contextualize June 2025 data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Florida dengue cases are predominantly travel-associated; understanding this baseline helps flag anomalies such as locally acquired clusters or outbreaks.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where dengue counts are aggregated with other arboviruses (West Nile, Zika, chikungunya) without dengue-specific breakdowns, or where reporting period substantially exceeds June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Arbovirus aggregate counts without dengue-specific figures must not be extracted as dengue records; sources with broad reporting periods require human judgment on date-window fit.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite case counts without traceable official provenance for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified figures; human review ensures only traceable, provenance-backed counts enter the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: FDOH publishes weekly and annual arbovirus surveillance reports including dengue case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable), travel status, and occasionally hospitalizations and deaths. CDC DVBD and ArboNET provide national-level data with state breakdowns. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for Florida dengue in June 2025.

PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological updates covering the Americas including the USA. WHO Disease Outbreak News may reference US dengue events. These provide independent validation of Florida case data.

HealthMap, ProMED-mail, Global Health Monitor, and open government data portals aggregate dengue event signals from official and news sources. These structured databases can validate FDOH/CDC primary data and surface county-level signals.

Peer-reviewed studies on Florida dengue epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology provide context for interpreting extracted counts. Recent publications may also contain 2025 case series or outbreak reports.

Local Florida news outlets (Miami Herald, Tampa Bay Times, Sun Sentinel) and health news aggregators may report dengue alerts, locally acquired case clusters, or FDOH press releases during June 2025, providing early signals and supporting evidence quotes.

input.user_request: Collect dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Florida from 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30.

structured_task.user_request: Collect dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Florida from 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30.

collection_spec.data_focus: human Dengue case, outbreak, and surveillance data
collection_spec.user_request: Collect dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Florida from 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30.

official_source_terms: Florida Department of Health arbovirus surveillance
likely_reporting_agencies: county health departments (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange)
count_semantics_notes: Strictly separate locally acquired (autochthonous) cases from travel-associated (imported) cases — Florida frequently reports both categories.
Dengue reports commonly use epidemiological (epi) weeks; map epi week to calendar date range for the 2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30 window (Epi Weeks 22–26 approximately).
Cumulative year-to-date counts must be distinguished from period-specific (June 2025) counts.
Confirmed vs. probable case definitions may differ between FDOH and CDC ArboNET; record the definition used.
County-level counts should be recorded separately from statewide totals when both are available.
Do not aggregate dengue counts with other arboviral diseases (Zika, chikungunya, West Nile) unless dengue-specific figures are explicitly broken out.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arbovirus counts (e.g., combined Zika + dengue + chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly reported.
Do not treat mosquito surveillance positivity (Aedes trap data) as human case counts.
Florida reports may include both travel-associated and locally acquired dengue — do not conflate these categories.
DENV serotype data (DENV-1 through DENV-4) should not be counted as separate case events.
ArboNET national totals must not be substituted for Florida-specific counts.
Hospitalization figures from clinical databases (e.g., discharge records) may differ from FDOH surveillance counts — note the source definition.
exclusion_terms: Aedes trap data without human cases
warnings: Florida dengue reports frequently distinguish travel-associated from locally acquired cases — both categories must be captured and labeled separately in collection records.
Epi week boundaries for June 2025 (approx. Epi Weeks 22–26) must be mapped to calendar dates before populating date_reported fields.
FDOH arbovirus surveillance reports may be published with a 1–2 week lag; the June 30 end date may not yet have a corresponding published report at time of collection.
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates — always filter or confirm Florida-specific figures before recording.
County-level dengue data may be suppressed in public FDOH reports for small counts (n<5) to protect patient privacy; record suppression explicitly rather than imputing zero.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Florida Department of Health (FDOH) arbovirus surveillance reports, weekly or monthly situation reports, and press releases reporting dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Florida during June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDOH is the primary official source for dengue case counts in Florida, publishing arbovirus surveillance summaries that include travel-associated and locally acquired dengue cases by county.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC Division of Vector-Borne Diseases (DVBD) reports, tables, or dashboards containing dengue case data for Florida for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and may contain Florida-specific dengue case counts, including confirmed and probable classifications.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify county-level health department reports (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange) with dengue case data for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: High-population Florida counties with international travel hubs are most likely to report dengue cases; county health departments may publish local arbovirus alerts or situation reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO or WHO situation reports, disease outbreak news, or regional surveillance bulletins referencing dengue in Florida or the USA for June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports provide independent validation of case counts and can confirm whether Florida-specific data is included in broader US or Americas summaries.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (HealthMap, ProMED, Global Health Monitor, or open data portals) with dengue event records for Florida in June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured surveillance databases aggregate official and news signals and can serve as independent validation against FDOH and CDC primary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or CDC case definitions establishing dengue confirmed, probable, and suspected classification criteria applicable to Florida surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition context is required to correctly interpret and normalize case classification fields (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) extracted from FDOH and CDC sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify background sources describing Florida's dengue epidemiology, including travel-associated vs. locally acquired case patterns, to contextualize June 2025 data.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Florida dengue cases are predominantly travel-associated; understanding this baseline helps flag anomalies such as locally acquired clusters or outbreaks.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources where dengue counts are aggregated with other arboviruses (West Nile, Zika, chikungunya) without dengue-specific breakdowns, or where reporting period substantially exceeds June 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Arbovirus aggregate counts without dengue-specific figures must not be extracted as dengue records; sources with broad reporting periods require human judgment on date-window fit.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite case counts without traceable official provenance for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified figures; human review ensures only traceable, provenance-backed counts enter the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: FDOH publishes weekly and annual arbovirus surveillance reports including dengue case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable), travel status, and occasionally hospitalizations and deaths. CDC DVBD and ArboNET provide national-level data with state breakdowns. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for Florida dengue in June 2025.

PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports and epidemiological updates covering the Americas including the USA. WHO Disease Outbreak News may reference US dengue events. These provide independent validation of Florida case data.

HealthMap, ProMED-mail, Global Health Monitor, and open government data portals aggregate dengue event signals from official and news sources. These structured databases can validate FDOH/CDC primary data and surface county-level signals.

Peer-reviewed studies on Florida dengue epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology provide context for interpreting extracted counts. Recent publications may also contain 2025 case series or outbreak reports.

Local Florida news outlets (Miami Herald, Tampa Bay Times, Sun Sentinel) and health news aggregators may report dengue alerts, locally acquired case clusters, or FDOH press releases during June 2025, providing early signals and supporting evidence quotes.
